gloss: from A to B, over the span of; when it comes to

definitions.gloss: from A through B; over the span of; across
definitions.explanation: Paired with から to mark a stretch of time or space treated as one continuous span: {春|はる}から{夏|なつ}にかけて (from spring through summer). The endpoints are approximate, so it suits vague ranges rather than exact schedules.

definitions.gloss: when it comes to; in terms of; at ~ nobody beats
definitions.explanation: In the pattern 〜にかけては, it names the area in which someone excels. Nearly always followed by a claim of superiority, so it reads as praise or a boast.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}から{夏|なつ}にかけて{咲|さ}く。
examples.english: It blooms from spring through summer.

examples.japanese: {今夜|こんや}から{明日|あす}の{朝|あさ}にかけて{雨|あめ}が{強|つよ}まるでしょう。
examples.english: The rain will intensify from tonight through tomorrow morning.

examples.japanese: {関東|かんとう}から{東北|とうほく}にかけての{広|ひろ}い{範囲|はんい}で、{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}ると{予想|よそう}されている。
examples.english: Snow is forecast over a wide area stretching from Kanto to Tohoku.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}の{速|はや}さにかけては{負|ま}けない。
examples.english: When it comes to running speed, I won't lose to anyone.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}にかけては{母|はは}にかなわない。
examples.english: When it comes to cooking, I'm no match for my mother.

examples.japanese: {記憶力|きおくりょく}にかけては、この{中|なか}で{彼女|かのじょ}の{右|みぎ}に{出|で}る{者|もの}はいない。
examples.english: When it comes to memory, nobody here can match her.

notes:
Sense 1 attaches to nouns of time or place and is normally paired with から; before a noun it becomes 〜にかけての. Sense 2 takes the は-marked form 〜にかけては and attaches to a skill or field.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- AからBにかけて: from A through B
- AからBにかけての〜: the ~ stretching from A to B
- 〜にかけては{誰|だれ}にも{負|ま}けない: nobody beats me at ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- 〜から〜まで: from ~ to ~ — marks exact endpoints; use it for {九時|くじ}から{五時|ごじ}まで, not にかけて
- 〜{間|あいだ}: during ~ — a period seen as a whole, without the sense of moving across it
